item.title: When weight regain in obesity means stigma and double standards
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Weight regain after discontinuing pharmacological treatment for obesity has again come into focus following a recent systematic review and meta-analysis published in BMJ[1]. The review shows that most individuals who stop these medications gradually regain the weight they had lost, alongside a reversal of many cardiometabolic benefits achieved during treatment. Importantly, this process is not marginal: on average, body weight returns to baseline within one to two years.

item.title: Informed Consent and the Risk of Sterility in the PATHWAYS Trial
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editors: The protocols for the PATHWAYS trial raise serious concerns about the possibility of genuinely informed consent on the issue of fertility. Puberty suppression disrupts the maturation of the reproductive system and loss of fertility is a known risk. What remains unclear is the extent to which fertility can be attained if puberty suppression is halted.
